tests.name: Test-design rationale
tests.description: Review tests against the requirements and a mutant that returns min+1 for value == min.
tests.expected: The lower-bound assertion rejects the mutant; branch coverage alone would not.

reasoning: For a closed interval, values on either boundary remain unchanged. A one-point interval maps every input to that one point.

The function has no console or file dependency. An assertion against an independently chosen expected value checks behavior; a test that merely calls the function or achieves high coverage can miss wrong results.
The JUnit excerpt uses genuine assertEquals/assertThrows contracts but is labelled unexecuted. Equivalent cases are checked by the trusted plain-Java development harness.
These are authored reference requirements and code. Revealing them does not run tests on your code or record broad skill correctness.
